headline: Medium prompt-injection and data-leakage risks from shared workspace flows and vendor-hosted Q&A; no critical path is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can ingest files and chain tools in server-side flows, while Notion AI reads workspace pages and returns grounded answers. A shared workspace or copied content can let attacker-controlled text from one agent influence the other’s instructions. The pathway exists in default-style deployments, though no direct shared channel is documented here, so uncertainty is resolved upward.
conditions: IF Langflow flow inputs include Notion-generated page text as prompt material
IF Notion pages contain attacker-authored instruction-like content that Langflow later parses
mitigations: Add a fixed delimiter and instruction hierarchy around imported text
Strip or escape prompt-like tokens before passing content between systems
Use a human review step before Langflow consumes Notion output
Restrict shared pages to trusted editors only
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to every cross-agent payload

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch workspace content and can send data to vendor backends: Langflow via configured model providers and arbitrary HTTP services, Notion AI via Notion vendor backends and downstream model providers. If the same sensitive workspace data is routed through both, leakage can occur across two third-party processing paths. The profiles do not prove PHI or secrets, so medium is the highest supported severity.
conditions: IF the same confidential document is loaded into Langflow and Notion AI
IF either agent forwards that content to a third-party model provider
mitigations: Limit both agents to non-sensitive test workspaces
Disable external model providers in Langflow for sensitive flows
Use Notion pages with minimal access scope
Redact secrets before copying content between tools
requires-engineering: enforce data-class routing policies

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow has server-side filesystem write and broad egress, while Notion AI has no host execution but does operate on shared workspace state across members. They do not both have unrestricted write to the same local directory, so high is not justified. Still, overlapping mutation of shared knowledge and flow state can create conflicts and stale writes in default deployments.
conditions: IF Langflow writes artifacts that are later mirrored into a shared Notion workspace
IF multiple users edit the same Notion pages while Langflow consumes them
mitigations: Separate draft and published workspaces
Lock shared pages during automated ingestion windows
Keep Langflow outputs in a dedicated folder or database
Review concurrent edits before syncing
requires-engineering: add optimistic locking across systems

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow can chain multiple agents and tools, and Notion AI is a RAG-style Q&A system grounded in workspace content. If Langflow output is treated as authoritative and then summarized or acted on in Notion, errors can propagate without verification. The pair lacks an explicit cross-check mechanism in the profiles, so a default medium-risk cascade is plausible.
conditions: IF Langflow-generated text is pasted into Notion as source material
IF Notion AI summarizes Langflow output without a verification step
mitigations: Require source citations before reuse
Add a manual fact-check step between agents
Mark Langflow outputs as draft-only
Use Notion pages for review, not execution
requires-engineering: implement provenance-aware verification

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI is vendor-hosted and processes workspace content under the invoking user’s Notion permissions, while Langflow can send flow inputs to arbitrary HTTP/model providers. If regulated or region-bound data is moved between them, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show a specific residency mismatch, so medium is the supported level.
conditions: IF EU or regulated data is entered into both systems
IF Langflow routes that data to a provider outside the required jurisdiction
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Use separate workspaces for regulated content
Review vendor DPAs and retention settings
Disable external providers for sensitive Langflow flows
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing controls
